entities.summary:
Meditation: Mental Practice of Focus on a Particular Object, Thought, or Activity\n
Meditation has its roots in ancient Eastern cultures, with evidence of mindfulness practices dating back to the Indus Valley Civilization (3300-1300 BCE) and the Vedic period in ancient India (1500-500 BCE).\n
The earliest known meditation practices in the Western world can be traced back to ancient Greece, where the philosopher Plato (427-347 BCE) wrote about the importance of contemplation and self-reflection in his works.\n
In the 20th century, meditation gained popularity in the West with the introduction of Transcendental Meditation (TM) by Maharishi Mahesh Yogi (1918-2008) in the 1950s. TM became a global phenomenon, with millions of practitioners worldwide.\n
Today, meditation is practiced by people from all walks of life, with various techniques and traditions, from mindfulness-based stress reduction to Kundalini yoga.\n
Meditation has had a profound impact on modern society, with benefits ranging from reduced stress and anxiety to improved mental clarity and focus.\n
Despite its long history, meditation remains a relatively understudied topic in Western academia, with more research needed to fully understand its effects on physical and mental health.
